name: Wulna
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2001. A grammar of Limilngan: a language of the Mary River region, Northern Territory, Australia. Pacific Linguistics 516. Canberra: ANU. ch.1, pp.5-8.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: On Wuna: Breen 1980 + Hale 1959 materials give 'an outline of the basic phonological and morphological structures of Wuna. However, these materials do not permit any detailed phonological or morphological analysis of Wuna'. The Van Diemen coast sprachbund (Gaagudju, Limilngan, Larrakia; Wuna 'presumably' a member) is said to show strong stressed/unstressed syllable differentiation with vowel reduction, but nothing is stated about stress position in Wuna.

sources.citation: Bennett, John William Ogilvie. 1869. Vocabulary of the Woolner District Dialect, Adelaide River, Northern Territory. Adelaide: W. C. Cox, Government Printer. (Paul Foelsche's annotated copy, SLNSW MLMSS 8070; 35 page images)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Observations' page: 'The short accent is marked thus [breve], (sometimes not marked). The long accent is marked thus -. In most cases the last syllable of a word, without the long accent, is almost silent.' -- 'accent' here = vowel-length diacritics; the only prosodic remark is that word-final syllables are nearly silent. No statement of where stress falls. Foelsche's handwritten additions place an apostrophe after the first syllable (Gwin'goot-lar, Coo'linyer, Co'moomber, May'nugger) -- raw data, no rule stated.
